title: What If Forest Elephants Went Extinct?

scenes.text: What if forest elephants disappeared? Scientists say the forest itself would change.
Forest elephants help more than a hundred tree species germinate by spreading their seeds across the forest.
They also thin out small, soft-wood trees, which leaves room for big hardwoods that store more carbon.
Without them, the forest slowly fills with smaller, lighter trees that hold far less carbon.
Simulations suggest Central African forests could lose up to three billion tons of carbon.
That's roughly what France emits in twenty-seven years, from losing a single animal.
